commit.message:
fix(transcoder): write empty VTT stub when provider returns no transcribable speech (#124)

Production effect: silent / music-only / non-speech videos used to surface
as HTTP 500 from the transcoder, which left no VTT object in GCS at all.
The edge then served `GET /{hash}/vtt` as 202 "in_progress" forever,
blocking any downstream consumer that polled until completion.

The provider response itself is correct in those cases — Parakeet (an
acoustic model) genuinely cannot produce text from silence/music, and
the existing `normalize_transcript_to_vtt` rightly rejects the empty
response so it doesn't render the raw JSON envelope as a fake VTT cue.
The bug was in the caller: it treated normalize errors uniformly as
failures rather than distinguishing "transcript empty (success, no
speech)" from "transcript failed (real error)".

Adds a small classifier `is_empty_transcript_normalize_error` that
matches the three normalize-side messages indicating an empty result.
process_transcribe now substitutes `ParsedVtt::empty(...)` when that
classifier fires, parallel to how the existing transcript-drop guards
(LowProviderConfidence, LowSignalHeuristic, LoopHallucination,
ImplausibleTextDensity) already do. Result: an empty `WEBVTT\n\n` is
written to GCS, the edge serves 200, and downstream consumers see
"transcribed, no captions" rather than "still pending."

Real provider failures (5xx, timeouts, JSON parse errors, missing
config) are NOT reclassified — those continue to webhook `failed` and
return Err to the caller as before.

Tests: classifier matches the three empty-content errors and rejects
five distinct real-failure shapes. Cargo suite: 116 passing.

Backstory: surfaced during the Parakeet backfill of 5,932 user-uploaded
videos since 2026-04-19. ~1,051 of them returned this code path
because the previous Gemini-2.5-Pro pipeline had been hallucinating
fake transcripts on silent/music audio. Their old VTTs were correctly
deleted during backfill, but no new VTT was written, leaving them
stuck in 202 in_progress state until this fix lands.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
